best_for: Developers who resolve merge conflicts by hand and want a free three-way diff tool that also compares whole folders, on Windows, Mac and Linux.

points.title: Three-way merges
points.text: KDiff3 compares and merges two or three text files or folders. Seeing the common base next to both changes makes it clearer which side to keep.

points.title: Down to the character
points.text: Differences show line by line and character by character, with options to highlight or hide whitespace and comment changes.

points.title: Merging that does some of the work
points.text: An automatic merge option settles the easy conflicts, and a built-in editor lets you fix the rest. It also handles version control keywords and history merging.

points.title: Encodings, network files, printing
points.text: It reads Unicode, UTF-8 and other encodings, can open files over the network through KDE's KIO, and prints the differences when you need them on paper.

points.title: Linux trails by a release
points.text: Windows and macOS are at 1.12.6 while the Linux Flatpak is at 1.12.5. The Windows installer can install per-user or for all users and the Windows listing keeps 19 versions; macOS (13 or later) and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Flatpak from KDE
points.text: The Flathub build is published by KDE and marked verified, for x64 and Arm64, at about 12 MB to download.
